text:
0.12 → 0.13 Upgrade Guide | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
Skip to content
Menu
Back to top
0.12 → 0.13 Upgrade guide
​
Warnings & known issues
​
Please remember to create a new instance of TFG and copy your world across into it, instead of upgrading it in-place!
This is both safer, and also lets you preview your upgraded world, so you can go back and prepare it better.
If you're upgrading from 0.11, please follow the
0.12 upgrade instructions first
.
Worlds from 0.12 are safe to update to 0.13, but there are some important things to know:
Overworld worldgen
​
Due to some issues with servers, we've changed the default world generation for worlds from pre-0.12 to the
new worldgen
.
If your world was created in 0.12 then you don't have to do anything.
If your world was created before 0.12 and you've already changed it to use the new worldgen, you don't have to do anything.
If your world was created before 0.12 and you want to keep the old worldgen, you will need to change the
worldgenOverrides
setting in
defaultconfigs/tfg-server.toml
to
["minecraft:overworld=0"]
.
You don't have to do anything to get the new mineshafts, just explore new chunks.
In the future (likely in several months) we may drop support for the old worldgen, as it is becoming a lot of work to keep both available.
Beneath overhaul
​
We've completely reworked the Beneath. It's now significantly taller, so you will need to wipe the dimension in order to not be teleported above bedrock.
To do this, first make a backup of your save, Next, make sure you've left the Beneath and taken anything with you that you want to keep, then save and quit your game. After, simply go to your minecraft instance folder, then inside
saves
, then inside the folder named after your save. Delete the folder called
DIM-1
. Then launch your game as normal. The process is the same for servers.
⚠ ⚠ ⚠
MAKE A BACKUP BEFORE DOING THIS
⚠ ⚠ ⚠
If you've ever opened an HV or LuV Prospector's
Fluid Mode
in the Beneath, or used a
Fluid Drilling Rig
, you will also need to delete your
.minecraft/saves/(world name)/data/gtceu_bedrock_fluid.dat
file, as the fluid veins have also changed.
Food rework
​
TFC Gourmet has been removed. If you've got any food or fluids from that mod, eat them before upgrading, as they will all disappear afterwards.
We will continue to add new foods (including some that TFC Gourmet added) as our own in-house items so we have full control over their implementation and balancing.
Fluid Logistics
​
Create: Factory Logistics
has been replaced with
Create Fluid Logistics
, a different fluid addon for Create's logistics system that's less buggy.
Jar packagers in your world should be automatically replaced with the new Fluid packagers, and Fluid Gauges should be automatically replaced with normal factory gauges, which can now handle fluids themselves).
If you use a lot of these, please triple check you've made a backup before updating!
Shaders
​
After updating, if your Beneath is entirely tinted red/orange, go to the shader settings > Atmosphere > The Nether Dimension > Color Mode, and change it to "Biome Based",
not
"Biome Based (Modified)". Alternatively, select a different preset if it says you have a "custom" one.
Ores
​
Naquadah has been removed from the Beneath. It has temporarily been moved to the Ostrum Linear Accelerator until it eventually finds a home on a future planet.
Chromium has been completely changed. Due to the introduction of gem slurries, Ruby became the king of both aluminium and chromium, which was an unintended side effect. To resolve this:
Ruby is now a significantly worse source of aluminium, but still a good source of chromium. It's also now a source of Alumina for circuit boards.
Garnet Sand has been massively buffed with its own processing line, involving Yellow Garnet and Uvarovite. You can find it in sandy places in the overworld, or in huge quantities at the bottom of the Beneath.
Chromite can be obtained through some ore processing, or you can find it and yellow garnet ores on the Moon.
You unlock easier ways of processing all three as you progress.
ComputerCraft
​
We've added a mod to enable UTF-8 support for ComputerCraft.
Existing ComputerCraft programs should continue to work without migration. Programs which already contain valid UTF-8 text should display correctly after installing the mod. Programs which were previously saved with corrupted/mojibake text will need that text corrected manually; simply opening and saving the file again will not automatically recover the original characters.

title: Update 0.13 | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
text:
Update 0.13 | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
Skip to content
Menu
Back to top
Major Release 0.13 Changelog
​
Warnings & known issues
​
As always--We recommend you download a new instance of TFG and copy your save files across (along with your xaeros folder, options.txt, etc) instead of updating directly in place. Also, make backups often!
WARNING! If you're upgrading your world from 0.12 to 0.13, please read the upgrade guide
here
.
Using the Beneath start seems to have some trouble involving using a bed to set your spawn.
There's a lot of null pointer exceptions being spammed in the log files. We're investigating what's causing them, but for the time being they seem to be harmless.
Concrete supports only support the same range as wood ones. Rebar/steel/reinforced concrete supports are unaffected
Some loot chests and vessels in the new towers are empty.
Major Changes
​
For minor changes and bug fixes, check out the
changelogs
.
Beneath
​
The Beneath has been totally remade! It's now significantly taller (208 blocks tall instead of 128), has almost twice as many biomes, its own new set of crops, fruit trees, and wood sets, new structures, and new challenges. It's been split into three layers instead of just two, with the different layers providing challenges for different stages of the game, from wrought iron age to LV/MV. Also, it's
actually
hot now - make sure you're prepared!
Because of the height change, you'll need to delete your generated chunks so you aren't sent above the bedrock roof. Please read our
upgrade guide
for instructions on how to do this.
Starting in the Beneath is now an option when creating a new world. For an extra challenge, it should be possible to get to HV without leaving! We'll work on improving this experience and providing some unique Beneath-only ways of getting resources in future updates.
Beneath ores and fluid veins have been reworked
Changed piglin bartering table so there's less junk
The blue steel diving set no longer makes you completely immune to hot temperatures, but it does still provide a lot of cooling and make you immune to fire damage
All aqueducts can now hold lava and different kinds of water
The Hellforge now works with any kind of aqueduct, only needs charcoal piles to build instead of Anthracite, and can heat 9 crucibles at once
Added new tameable/ranchable slimes, for an alternative way to obtain certain resources
Added a new quest chapter for the Beneath
Food rework
​
A substantial rework of food and nutrition has been started. You will begin to notice a lot of new nutrition types have been added. There are now two new categories of nutrients: "Contaminants" and "Transient Effects". Contaminants build up when eating certain foods and can be cured by consuming new capsule medication. Transient effects apply 1 time buffs/debuffs when consuming food. Both of these new nutrient types can merged into dynamic meal items.
In addition to that, now each nutrient type has a special buff on the player when a certain threshold is crossed, such as >85% fruit nutrition granting a passive 30% mining speed buff. You can learn more about all of the nutrition changes by checking out the improved nutrition screen or by reading the
Food and Water
section of the field guide.
On top of the nutrition rework, we are also making a large balance pass on our food items. It is not possible to list every change here. But the major change is that the TFC Gourmet mod is being removed and replaced with our own built-in food items. This is due to buggy interactions and lack of support from the developer. Most new food items will come in a future update. This update will only include Fruit Juice, Smoothies, and Yogurts.
Fluid Logistics
​
Create: Factory Logistics
has been replaced with
Create Fluid Logistics
, a different fluid addon for Create's logistics system that's less buggy.
Jar packagers in your world should be automatically replaced with the new Fluid packagers, and Fluid Gauges should be automatically replaced with normal factory gauges, which can now handle fluids themselves).
If you use a lot of these, please triple check you've made a backup before updating!
Ores
​
Most ores have received a new coat of paint, improving their item and block textures, corresponding with their real-world crystal structure.
Added a new multiblock that exclusively works at the bottom of the Beneath - the
Geologic Vulcanizer
. Right now, it can process all your ores in one single recipe
and
return a bit of extra than you'd normally get doing all the steps separately! However, it's significantly more complicated to run... check the quest in LV for more details.
Naquadah has been removed from the Beneath. It has temporarily been moved to the Ostrum Linear Accelerator until it eventually finds a home on a future planet.
Chromium has been completely changed. Due to the introduction of gem slurries, Ruby became the king of both aluminium and chromium, which was an unintended side effect. To resolve this:
Ruby is now a significantly worse source of aluminium, but still a good source of chromium. It's also now a source of Alumina for circuit boards.
Garnet Sand has been massively buffed with its own processing line, involving Yellow Garnet and Uvarovite. You can find it in sandy places in the overworld, or in huge quantities at the bottom of the Beneath.
Chromite can be obtained through some ore processing, or you can find it and yellow garnet ores on the Moon.
You unlock easier ways of processing all three as you progress.
New Structures
​
Added mineshaft structures to the overworld! These are
guaranteed
to contain ore veins and are a great way to explore more of the overworld's caves.
Added new structures to the Beneath, including a large tower structure for easier vertical navigation, and an abandoned house near the top layer.
New Tools
​
Added a Wireless Charger to charge items and equipment around your base!
Added a Chameleon Spray Can, a spray can that can do all colors in one item, as well as some extra text effects on signs.
Shaders
​
After updating, if your Beneath is entirely tinted red/orange, go to the shader settings > Atmosphere > The Nether Dimension > Color Mode, and change it to "Biome Based",
not
"Biome Based (Modified)". Alternatively, select a different preset if it says you have a "custom" one.
Other mod updates
​
Added optional compatibility for
Immersive Vehicles
with the
MTS Official Content Pack
and
MTS Official Automobile Pack
Added
Create Stock Bridge
, which lets your create logistics network talk to your AE2 network (it caused a crash with the previous fluid logistics mod)
TFC Ambiental
has been forked into TFG-Core, so we can better optimize it and extend it
Temporarily removing the
Waves
mod to investigate a potential chunk corruption bug. Feel free to re-add it if you want

Skip to content

Back to top
Optional Mods
​
Here's some more mods that are compatible with TFG but aren't included by default. Feel free to add them to your own instance of the modpack!
Visual
​
Distant Horizons
(
CF
,
MR
) - TFG comes with configurations to get it working with TFC's world generation. IMPORTANT: DH will be unable to generate LODs unless the mod Chunky is removed.
BlueMap
- TFG comes with a resource pack for it to work with some of TFC's blocks.
Third Person
​
Shoulder Surfing Reloaded
(
CF
,
MR
) - Improved third person camera mod. Client-side, so you can install it even if you're playing on someone else's server.
Third Person Shooting: Zero
(
CF
,
MR
) - Adds compatibility between Shoulder Surfing Reloaded and TACZ (the gun mod)
Resource Packs
​
ILAORE's 32x Texture Packs
- for
TFC
,
Create
,
AE2
, and
GregTech
. If you like higher detailed textures, you might like one of these, but keep in mind that a lot of blocks in TFG do not have 32x versions so there will be some style clashing.
Ad Astra 3D
(
CF
,
MR
) - Replaces the usual pixelated textures of the celestial bodies in different sky boxes with 3D models. Goes great with shaders!
HotOrNot 3D Mittens
(
MR
) - Changes the appearance of the TFC HotOrNot mittens into a 3D model.
Naturalis
(
CF
,
MR
) - Makes fruit trees and grain crops more "bushy" looking.
TFC Livestock Skins
(
CF
) - Adds some variations of livestock animals like alpacas, chickens, and ducks, based on the climate and block they spawned on. Requires
ETF
and
EMF
to be installed as well.
lsc's Player Dolls
(
CF
,
MR
) - A simple resource pack that transforms vanilla Player Heads into adorable dolls. Put a plushie of GregT next to your EBF! Requires
ETF
and
EMF
to be installed as well.
Content
​
Addons
​
Epic Knights of TerraFirmaGreg
(
CF
) - Adds additional weapons and armor to the TFC era of the modpack. Not included by default because of a lot of extra equipment bloat.
Via Romana
: (
CF
) - Adds infrastructure driven fast travel. Allowing you create road networks with signs to travel between locations. TFG includes a built in
config file
for allowing roads to be made out of many of our blocks.
With Custom Recipes
​
Create: Sound of Steam
(
CF
,
MR
) - expands on create's Steam Whistle and adds a ton more options to let you play music. Not included by default because of how niche it is. We include our own recipes for it though.
Chimes
(
CF
) - adds some wind chimes. Not included by default to avoid modpack bloat, but we do have our own recipes for it.
Create: Extra Gauges
(
CF
,
MR
) - expands on create's factory gauges. If you add it to your modpack, you'll get TFG recipe changes.
Create: Railways Navigator
(
CF
,
MR
) - Expands on train scheduling, adds passenger information displays for both trains and stations, and includes a navigator device that can tell you which trains to board for your intended journey. Not included by default because it primarily benefits large, rail-heavy multiplayer servers. Custom recipes included.
Dragonlib
(
CF
,
MR
) - A library required for Railways Navigator to work.
IMPORTANT:
The latest version of dragonlib has been found to prevent the game from loading. Versions 3.0.21 and 3.0.26 have both been reported to work.

title: Updating & Reinstalling the Modpack | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
text:
Updating & Reinstalling the Modpack | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
Skip to content
Menu
Back to top
Updating and Reinstalling the Modpack
​
When updating the modpack, it is always safest to do so through a
clean reinstall
. If your modpack launcher has an "update" button, this frequently does not update the modpack correctly, leading to broken recipes, the modpack failing to launch, and other issues.
If your modpack has a strange bug that nobody else seems to have, often a
clean reinstall
will fix the problem. It's a good idea to try this before
reporting it to us
.
How to do a clean reinstall
​
Prism
​
Click the "Add Instance" button at the top of the window.
Go to the CurseForge section and download TerraFirmaGreg-Modern.
Wait for the modpack to download and install.
If it asks if you want to create a new instance or to update, select
Create Instance
.
When you get a "Blocked mods found" window, follow the instructions to download the remaining mods.
After the download is finished, select the new instance and press the "Folder" button on the right. Select the old instance and do the same. Go inside the
minecraft
folders in each.
CurseForge
​
Select your existing instance, then click the "Change Versions" button with the two arrows next to the orange Play button.
Make sure "Update to latest version" is selected, then tick the box for "Update to a separate modpack profile".
Wait for the modpack to download and install.
After the download is finished, select the new instance, then open the triple-dot menu on the top right, then select Open Folder. Select the old instance and do the same.
Next Steps
​
Copy and paste these folders and files from your old folder into the new one:
saves
xaero
backups
(optional)
options.txt
emi.json
(if it exists)
emi.css
(if it exists)
Change the new instance's maximum RAM allocation to what you had before (we recommend 6-8 GB)
Launch the new instance as normal. Check that everything works properly before deleting your old instance!
Servers
​
Download and extract the server pack from our
GitHub
.
Copy the new server pack files into your server, but into a separate folder from your current install.
Copy and paste the
saves
and
backups
(optional) folders from your old instance into your new one, as well as anything else server-specific like the player whitelist.
Launch the new instance as normal. Check that everything works properly before deleting your old instance!
Your players will need to be on the same version in order to connect to your server. If they have an error about mod version mismatches (even if the mod versions look the same), that usually means they did not update correctly, and you should send them a link to this guide.

title: 0.11 → 0.12 Upgrade guide | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
text:
0.11 → 0.12 Upgrade guide | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
Skip to content
Menu
Back to top
0.11 → 0.12 Upgrade guide
​
Warnings & known issues
​
Please remember to create a new instance of TFG and copy your world across into it, instead of upgrading it in-place!
This is both safer, and also lets you preview your upgraded world, so you can go back and prepare it better.
If you're upgrading from 0.10, please follow the
0.11 upgrade instructions first
.
Worlds from 0.11 are safe to update to 0.12, but there are some important things to know:
New Fluid Veins
​
We have completely redone the overworld fluid veins so some of them depend on climate and biome. As a consequence, the fluid veins you used to have around your base will likely be different than before. Check out the new EMI tab to find out where to find new good veins you can move your fluid rigs to.
If your chunks have no fluid at all, try closing your game, deleting your
.minecraft/saves/(world name)/data/gtceu_bedrock_fluid.dat
file, and then launching your game again. This clears gregtech's cache of fluid veins, forcing it to generate new ones.
New Worldgen
​
0.12 has
new overworld world generation
. You do not have to make a new world to update.
If you have an
old
world and you want to continue using
old
worldgen
​
You don't have to do anything. Your world will continue to generate new chunks with the old worldgen, though it will have some of the new things like new crops and fluid vein features.
If you have an
old
world and you want to use the
new
worldgen
​
Open the
defaultconfigs/tfg-server.toml
file, and at the very bottom, replace
worldgenOverrides = []
with
worldgenOverrides = ["minecraft:overworld=1"]
.
You will need to make sure your config has this line every time you update in the future.
Note that this
will
cause ugly chunk boundaries. The shape of continents is roughly the same, so if this is something you care about, generate your whole continent before upgrading, so then the chunk borders will be in the ocean.
⚠ ⚠ ⚠
MAKE A BACKUP BEFORE DOING THIS
⚠ ⚠ ⚠
If you want to make a
new
world with
new
worldgen
​
Just create a new world as usual. Your world will remember that it was created in the new worldgen and you don't have to touch any configs.
If you want to make a
new
world with
old
worldgen
​
Create your world in 0.11.28, then update. Or start in 0.12 but set
worldgenOverrides = ["minecraft:overworld=0"]
before generating a world.
Custom Spawn Locations
​
When creating your world, you are now able to select where your worldspawn will be. On a multiplayer server, all players will spawn at this spawn point like they would normally.
Note that TFC is still changing its 1.21 worldgen, and we will be backporting future changes.

title: 0.10 → 0.11 Upgrade Guide | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
text:
0.10 → 0.11 Upgrade Guide | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
Skip to content
Menu
Back to top
0.10 → 0.11 Upgrade guide
​
Please remember to create a new instance of TFG and copy your world across into it, instead of upgrading it in-place!
This is both safer, and also lets you preview your upgraded world, so you can go back and prepare it better.
If you're upgrading from 0.9, please follow the
0.10 upgrade instructions first
.
Worlds from 0.10 are safe to update to 0.11, but there are a few minor breaking changes:
A significant amount of EV progression has been reworked:
Almost every recipe related to uranium/plutonium/radon has been changed, and now requires Fission on Mars.
Nano CPU Wafers now require a product at the end of the Fission progression.
Tungsten now has a new (and more complicated) refinement process.
Windmills and Water wheels are now Greate tiered, and water wheels now require a river to work at their full effectiveness. If you were using them "properly", as in, in a river for your steam age progression, you should be mostly unaffected by this change. If you were spamming tons of them off of placed water sources in your basement, move to a different power source! To help balance this, windmill sails are now even cheaper, and blaze burners are available in the steel age.
The Programmed Circuit Card mod has been removed. This will affect any AE2 setups you have using it, and instead you should use different machines for each circuit (or upgrade to the IV multiblock). We do want to minimize the pain with this though, so if you need a whole assembler for one obscure circuit number for one recipe, please
let us know
and we'll switch the numbers around.
The Netherarium and Enderarium have been removed. You will be able to get all their important outputs from Mars. If you have any nether/ender air stored, distill it because those recipes will be going away soon too.
Processed thorium items like ingots, rods, etc have been removed. Macerate them all into dust first!
If you still have any old "replace me" items from your 0.7 to 0.9 upgrade, they will be deleted, so be sure to convert them all!
Raw rubber ingots have been removed.

title: 0.9 → 0.10 Upgrade Guide | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
text:
0.9 → 0.10 Upgrade Guide | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
Skip to content
Menu
Back to top
0.9 → 0.10 Upgrade guide
​
Please remember to create a new instance of TFG and copy your world across into it, instead of upgrading it in-place!
This is both safer, and also lets you preview your upgraded world, so you can go back and prepare it better.
If you're upgrading from 0.7, please follow the
0.9 upgrade instructions first
.
Worlds from 0.9 are safe to update to 0.10, but there are a few minor breaking changes:
Refrigerators have been replaced with a new gregtech version that has different tiers, understands EU/t, and supports automation. You'll be able to convert your old refrigerator into the new one, but it will lose its contents. Take everything out of your fridge before updating!
Almost all automated food-related recipes have been moved to the new Food Processor and Food Oven machines.
Several ores have been moved around, most notably certus quartz and the aluminium/bauxite/ilmenite vein are now only on the moon. Check your field guide for more information.
Centrifuging quartz sand now gives nether quartz instead of certus quartz. If you want infinite certus quartz, check out the moon.
Chorus fruit can now only be grown on the moon in an electric greenhouse instead of irradiating regular fruit.
Lava from a hose pulley is no longer infinite. You can still use it as a fuel, but there's several other early game options to try out as well: creosote (from wood or coal), oilsands, or seed oil (and bio diesel) from new Sunflower and Rapeseed plants!
Almost every AE2-related recipe has been changed, so you will need to update all of your patterns.
Steam 'n' Rails is currently on an alpha version for Create 6 support, so some of your trains/bogeys may be invisible or glitchy.
GregTech has had a major version release with several breaking changes, so check out its
changelog
as well.
Check out the
TFG changelog
for a full list of all the other changes.

title: 0.7 → 0.9 Upgrade Guide | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
text:
0.7 → 0.9 Upgrade Guide | TerraFirmaGreg Wiki
Skip to content
Menu
Back to top
0.7 → 0.9 Upgrade guide
​
Please remember to create a new instance of TFG and copy your world across into it, instead of upgrading it in-place!
This is both safer, and also lets you preview your upgraded world, so you can go back and prepare it better.
Worlds from 0.7 should be mostly safe to upgrade to 0.9, but there are a few things you should know:
GregTech has removed all of its kinetic machines. If you're using kinetic input hatches, kinetic mixers, gear boxes (the GT kind, not the Create kind), or the alternator, these will all disappear when upgrading, so you should recycle them in an arc furnace or macerator first.
0.9 uses Greate, a Create addon that adds GregTech tiering to its mechanical components, so you'll have to replace any Create contraptions with equivalent versions. All of the old Create items are convertible to their Greate equivalents by placing them in a crafting grid. Greate's components have stress capacities so you may have to redo any large Create setups too. The GregTech Alternator and Gear Box can be replaced with Create: Additions' Alternator and Electric Motor.
Several ingots, plates, and raw ores have been changed to use a different item instead of the GregTech generated ones. These items have a "REPLACE ME" texture, and you can put them in a crafting grid to change them to the new versions.
Tree taps have changed to use ArborFirmaCraft instead. You should be able to replace your old taps with the new ones by putting them in a crafting grid and collecting latex in a wooden barrel instead of a bucket. The mechanics around when trees are tappable have changed too, check the field guide for more information -- there's several new tappable trees that you can use to get sticky resin now that may be more suitable for your climate.
Early quest chapters have been completely overhauled, so if losing your "progress" is something you care about, you can force-complete the quests by turning on cheats, then clicking the pencil on the bottom right of the quest screen, and right-clicking > Force Complete on the quests or chapters.
A single block of lava is no longer considered infinite via a hose pulley -- you'll need 2000 instead. Most of the lava lakes down at Y=-55 or so should be big enough though! Alternatively, the large boilers are also much more efficient now, so just two coke ovens processing logs are enough to power an EBF -- more if you use coal! And lastly, if you're in HV or above, you can try out the new Aqueous Accumulator machine to get infinite lava from just two source blocks.
If you're in the middle of the steam age, we strongly recommend getting into LV before upgrading, as the steam age progression has been significantly changed.
